note: Chat link spans and card eligibility. Offsets are UTF-16 code units, half-open. `url` is the resolved URL (https:// prepended when the match had no scheme). `card` is null or the first card-eligible Flipcash link in the message, with its jump wrapper already unwrapped. `card` is null, the first Flipcash card in the message, or else the first https span whose host is outside cardHosts and eligible (see link_metadata.json hosts), with kind `web`. A card-host span that does not classify never becomes a web card, except on flipcash.com and www.flipcash.com (P25): there it is a web card unless its first path segment is login, verify, c or cash, or it has a fragment. A match whose following character is non-ASCII is rejected. Behavior parity, not a computation with an external reference.

vectors.name: text-around-link
vectors.note: Card above, this whole string as the caption beneath it.

vectors.name: two-links-one-card
vectors.note: Both links are tappable spans; the first card-eligible one wins.

vectors.name: bare-domain
vectors.note: No scheme: still a link, resolved with https://. A marketing-host page, so a web card (P25).

vectors.name: app-host-cash-link
vectors.note: Both hosts and both path spellings reach the same route.

vectors.name: jump-wrapped-cash-link
vectors.note: The card's url is the unwrapped target; resolution needs that, not the redirector.

vectors.name: glued-emoji-host
vectors.note: No span at all. The trailing character is non-ASCII, so the match is rejected: iOS by authorityIsASCII, Android by the boundary rule.

vectors.name: lookalike-host
vectors.note: Not a Flipcash card: the host is not in cardHosts. It is an outside link, so it gets the web card any outside link gets, and that card shows send.flipcash.com.evil.com as its domain. Showing the real host is the defence.

vectors.name: login-link
vectors.note: Carries the account seed. Never a card, whatever the host says.

vectors.name: verify-link
vectors.note: Carries a verification secret. Never a card.

vectors.name: tip-card-by-id
vectors.note: A person card by user id. Shipped on both apps ahead of this fixture.

vectors.name: token-link
vectors.note: A token link renders as that token's bill. The mint is taken from the path and is not validated here -- an unknown mint is a card that never resolves, not a rejected one.

vectors.name: uppercase-scheme
vectors.note: A scheme matches in any case and resolves lowercase. Android used to prepend a second scheme (https://HTTPS://...), which parsed with HTTPS as the host; NSDataDetector hands the scheme back as written, so iOS lowercases it itself.

vectors.name: mixed-case-scheme
vectors.note: Only the scheme is lowercased. The rest of the URL is kept as written.

vectors.name: trailing-full-stop
vectors.note: A full stop ending the sentence is not part of the link. Kept, it would land in the cash link's fragment, after the entropy.

vectors.name: trailing-punctuation-run
vectors.note: A run of dropped characters is dropped whole: . , ; ! and a double quote.

vectors.name: bracketed-link
vectors.note: A closing bracket the link did not open belongs to the sentence.

vectors.name: balanced-brackets-kept
vectors.note: A closing bracket the link opened is part of it. The full stop after it is not. An outside https link, so a web card.

vectors.name: trailing-question-mark-kept
vectors.note: ? and : stay in the link, because NSDataDetector keeps them (it reads a trailing ? as an empty query). Pinned so neither side drops more than the other.

vectors.name: single-quoted-link
vectors.note: A single quote is dropped only when one opened the link. Unopened, it stays, as NSDataDetector keeps it.

vectors.name: bold-wrapped-link
vectors.note: Formatting markers follow the single-quote rule: a trailing * is dropped when a * directly precedes the link, so *example.com/foo* is bold around a whole link (text-format spec, decision 1).

vectors.name: italic-wrapped-link
vectors.note: The same for _.

vectors.name: strike-wrapped-link
vectors.note: The same for ~.

vectors.name: bold-wrapped-cash-link
vectors.note: Trimming the marker keeps it out of the entropy, so the card still forms. The bold around a card link is then not applied (text-format spec, decision 4).

vectors.name: unopened-trailing-marker-kept
vectors.note: With no marker before the link, a trailing * stays, as it does for a single quote. Patterns.WEB_URL and NSDataDetector both keep * _ and ~ at the end of a path (NSDataDetector checked on macOS 27).

vectors.name: mismatched-marker-kept
vectors.note: Only the marker that opened is dropped. A _ before the link does not drop a trailing *.

vectors.name: bare-domain-trailing-underscore
vectors.note: A bare domain glued to a trailing _ is not a link. NSDataDetector returns nothing here (macOS 27); Android rejects the match to agree (text-format spec, decision 1).

vectors.name: bare-domain-underscore-no-opener
vectors.note: The same without an opening _.

vectors.name: inner-marker-kept
vectors.note: Only the last character is trimmed; a marker inside the path stays.

vectors.name: group-invite
vectors.note: A bare /chat/<uuid> on a card host is a group card.

vectors.name: web-link
vectors.note: An outside https link is a web card. The card draws under the text; the span stays.

vectors.name: web-link-bare-domain
vectors.note: A bare domain resolves with https://, so it can be a web card.

vectors.name: http-link-no-card
